qt: to the Commission Ioan-Rareş Bogdan (PPE) Subject:

I welcome the European Commission’s efforts to reduce the Union’s strategic dependencies and ensure the supply of essential resources to industry. That said, I hold that establishing a European critical raw materials corporation harbours major pitfalls for resource-rich Member States, one of which is the possibility that Brussels takes charge of decisions concerning resource exploitation, a move that would infringe upon the sovereignty of Member States over their own subsoil – a principle that is enshrined in the Treaties. Other potential issues include the possibility that Eastern countries like Romania are relegated to the role of exporters of inexpensive raw ore to major Western industrial conglomerates, and the absence of clear guarantees that local communities will be in charge of processing and refining the minerals in question and that they will benefit from the added value generated by these extraction operations. In view of the above, could the Commission clarify: 1.
How it will guarantee that Romania’s exclusive sovereignty over its own mineral resources (graphite, copper, magnesium, rare earth elements) pursuant to Article 194(2) TFEU is upheld?

What binding mechanisms will be included in the future corporation’s charter in order to ensure that processing and refining operations are undertaken in the Member State where raw materials are extracted, and are not the exclusive preserve of major Western industrial hubs?
How it will ensure that European funding is not limited to supporting primary extraction, but also finances the full development of local high-value-added processing chains?
